samples.text:
The pie charts shows what types of accommodation international tourists used in one country in 2008 and in 2023.

In 2008, hotels was the most popular type with 55% of tourists, it was more than half. Staying with friends or relatives was 17%. Hostels and campsites had the same, 10% each, and rented apartments was the least popular with only 8%. It shows that hotels was much more popular than any other type in 2008.

In 2023, hotels was still the most popular but the percentage fell to 39%. The biggest change was the rented apartments, they increased from 8% to 31%, so they became the second. However, the other types decreased a little. Friends and relatives went down to 15%, hostels to 8% and campsites to 7%.

Overall, most of tourists stayed in the hotels in both years, but in 2023 many more tourists chose rented apartments than before. The other kinds of accommodation did not change very much during this time.
samples.why: Main changes covered with accurate figures · overview present but late · linking is simple and sometimes repetitive · adequate vocabulary · several agreement, article and punctuation errors that do not affect understanding.

samples.text:
The pie charts illustrate the types of accommodation used by international tourists visiting one country in 2008 and 2023.

Overall, hotels were the most popular form of accommodation in both years, although their share fell considerably. The most significant change was the dramatic rise in the popularity of rented apartments, while the other types of accommodation all declined slightly.

In 2008, more than half of international tourists (55%) stayed in hotels. Staying with friends or relatives was the second most common option, at 17%, while hostels and campsites each accounted for 10%. Rented apartments were the least popular choice, used by only 8% of visitors.

By 2023, the proportion of tourists staying in hotels had dropped to 39%. In contrast, the share using rented apartments rose sharply to 31%, which was almost four times the 2008 figure, and this category became the second most popular. The remaining types of accommodation saw small decreases: the figure for friends or relatives fell to 15%, hostels to 8% and campsites to 7%, making campsites the least used option.
samples.why: Clear overview of the main trends · key features well presented with accurate figures and a correct derived comparison · logical progression · range of cohesive devices · good vocabulary · mostly error-free.

samples.text:
The charts compare the types of accommodation chosen by international tourists in one country in 2008 and 2023.

While hotels remained the most common choice throughout, their lead was greatly reduced by the rapid growth of rented apartments, which had become a serious rival by 2023. All the other forms of accommodation lost a small amount of ground.

In 2008, hotels were used by 55% of international visitors, over three times as many as those staying with friends or relatives (17%). Hostels and campsites were each chosen by a tenth of tourists, and rented apartments were the least popular option, accounting for just 8%.

Fifteen years later, the proportion staying in hotels had declined by 16 percentage points to 39%. Rented apartments were the clear winners over the period, their share almost quadrupling to 31%, which meant that the gap between hotels and apartments had narrowed from 47 points to only 8. Meanwhile, the remaining categories each dipped slightly: staying with friends or relatives fell to 15%, hostels to 8% and campsites to 7%, so campsites went from joint third place to become the least popular type of accommodation.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected · clear overview · accurate figures used selectively with precise derived comparisons · cohesion managed skilfully · wide, precise vocabulary · varied, error-free structures.
